info.title: Opportunity Engine · initial internal API
info.description: Generated from the build kit's M1 contract plus contracts/overlay.json. This is the Brand Consistency Scanner's API; the capability beneath it is the Consistency Engine, whose detector namespace is CE-. Implemented detectors: CE-LINK-01, CE-ASSET-01, CE-DATA-01 (accepted also under their handoff names). Adds the M2 offer catalogue, the M3 requested-intake surface and protected report delivery, and the M4 engagement lifecycle. Operations under /public and /r have no authenticated actor and carry x-protected-by instead of x-minimum-role. Contract only; an operation appearing here is not a claim that a deployment serves it.

get.summary: The report as a page, for the person it is about
get.description: No authentication. Server-rendered HTML with no script, outside the operator application because that sits behind Cloudflare Access in production and a customer must never need to get past Access to read their own report. Every failure — expired, revoked, mistyped, another workspace's, never issued — renders the same page, which says nothing about whether a report exists. Contract only; not a claim this endpoint exists.

200.description: The report page.

404.description: The same page for every kind of unusable link. Deliberately identical to a 200 in everything except status and content, so a prober learns nothing from either.

get.summary: The embeddable request form, as a script
get.description: No authentication. One script tag and one container element on a venture's own site. It derives the origin it posts to from its own URL rather than from an attribute, so an embedding page cannot point it at another workspace; it renders the channel's purpose text as text rather than supplying its own; and it writes into a Shadow DOM so neither it nor the host page can restyle the other. Contract only; not a claim this endpoint exists.

AccessSession.name: CF_Authorization
AccessSession.description: Browser transport. Worker validates trusted Access assertion/JWT then resolves app membership; cookie/header presence alone grants no access.

implemented_detectors.description: Detectors this deployment actually runs. The operator displays this rather than a constant compiled into its bundle, so the interface cannot claim a capability the server does not have.

observation.description: What the collector recorded about this observation: status, role classification, rendered outcome, timing. Only fields this system produced; never page content or scraped text.

OfferPrice.description: A commercial price in MINOR units of its currency. Deliberately not Money: Money carries provider cost in micro-units of the ledger currency, and the two must never be added. The differing field names make a mix-up a schema error rather than an arithmetic one.

Offer.description: A catalogue entry at one version. Scope is defined by the catalogue; price is set by an owner approval. An entry with no approved price is visible but not sellable.

OfferMatch.description: Which catalogue scopes a case's CONFIRMED findings are eligible for. Deterministic and rule-based: the price and scope come from the catalogue, never from generation. When nothing matches, route_to_manual_quotation is true, which is an answer rather than a failure.

OfferDraft.description: A scope drafted for one case at one catalogue version. The price and scope are a snapshot: a later catalogue change does not reprice a draft already given.

CreateOfferDraft.description: Names the catalogue entry to draft. No price field: a caller cannot supply one, because a price that did not come from an owner approval is not a price this system will quote.

OfferPrerequisite.description: A condition about the customer that no capture can establish — authorized access, an agreed destination, a scope approval. Somebody records it and is named for recording it, the same shape as a review. Revoked entries are kept: what was claimed stays readable.

RecordOfferPrerequisite.description: The note is required and is the evidence for the claim: who granted what, when and how it was confirmed. A prerequisite recorded without one is an assertion with nothing behind it.

ScanTimeline.description: Everything recorded for one scan: which steps ran and how they ended, the evidence captured, and the findings derived from it. The reviewer's working view.

Review.description: One review decision, bound to the finding version it was made against. Immutable: a later decision is a new record, never an edit of this one.

IntakeForm.description: What a venture's public form must display before it may accept a submission: the scope and limits the requester is agreeing to, and the checks this channel offers.

SubmitIntakeRequest.description: A request for a check. Note what is absent: no tenant, no venture, no account and no price. The workspace comes from the host the request arrives on, never from this body.

authority_claim.description: What the requester asserts about their authority over the target. Recorded as a claim, never treated as proof: an owner still records the account and the authorization before anything is captured.

PublicIntakeRequest.description: What a member of the public may learn about their own request. Deliberately coarse: 'closed' covers both declined and expired, because a decline is an internal judgement that may be about the requester.

local_verification_code.description: Only ever non-null under the local fixture channel, which sends nothing. A deployed build has no code-returning channel.

IntakeRequest.description: The operator's view of a request, including the contact address needed to answer it. Reviewer and above; a viewer sees the queue without the address.

ReportGrant.description: A link to one report version, for one recipient, for a bounded time. Not a membership: it opens that version and nothing else — not the scan, not the evidence artifacts, not the account, not another report. The token itself is never in this shape; it is returned once, at issue.

IssuedReportGrant.description: The one and only response carrying the token. It is not stored in a readable form and cannot be retrieved again by any operation; losing it means issuing a new grant and revoking this one.

IssueReportGrant.description: No expiry field: the lifetime is fixed by the server, so a link cannot be issued that outlives what anybody decided. No address field either — the recipient reference is opaque-keyed before storage and the note is what an operator reads.

DeliveredReport.description: What the holder of a link may read: the rendered report body as it was published, and nothing that would let them reach anything else. No account id, no scan id, no evidence ids, no artifact URLs, no reviewer identity.

Engagement.description: Work somebody agreed to buy, against one drafted scope. There is no scope field to edit: a draft is immutable, so a changed scope means a new draft and a new engagement. Acceptance is a time, a note saying how it was obtained, and the member attesting to it — never a payment event.

AdvanceEngagement.description: acceptance_note is required exactly on the transition that first leaves the pre-acceptance states, and refused on every other — sending it where it does not belong is an error rather than ignored, so nobody believes they recorded an acceptance that is not there.

EngagementEvent.description: One transition, append-only. The state says where a thing is; this says how it got there, which is what a dispute needs.

PaymentRecord.description: What somebody typed about money. No card data, no processor token, no webhook. It moves no state: a payment is evidence money arrived, not evidence work was accepted.
